blocks.prompt: 4. Find all points on the ellipse \(x^{2} - xy + y^{2} = 1\) at which the tangent line is horizontal.
blocks.explanation:
Horizontal tangent ka matlab \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\), aur ellipse implicit shakal mein diya gaya hai.
Diya kya hai? Ellipse \(x^{2} - xy + y^{2} = 1\).
Find kya karna hai? Ellipse ke woh saare points jahan tangent leti hui ho.
Rule kaunsa? Implicit differentiation; \(xy\) ke liye product rule.
Plan: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikalo, numerator zero karo to ek rishta \(y = 2x\) milega; usse ellipse ki equation ke saath hal karo.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x^{2} - xy + y^{2} = 1\) ...(1).
Maloom karna: (1) ke woh tamam points jahan tangent horizontal ho.
Tareeqa: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) chahiye. (1) ko implicit differentiate karenge (\(xy\) par product rule), numerator ko zero karenge, aur jo rishta mile usse (1) ke saath solve karenge.

(1) ko \(x\) ke lehaz se differentiate karein
\[2x - \left(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\right) + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]
\[(2y - x)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y - 2x\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y - 2x}{2y - x}\]
Kyun: \(xy\) do functions ka product hai, is liye \(\frac{d}{dx}(xy) = x\frac{dy}{dx} + y\cdot 1\). Aur \(\frac{d}{dx}y^{2} = 2y\frac{dy}{dx}\) (chain rule). Phir \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) wali terms ek taraf aur baqi doosri taraf.
Dhyan dein: \(xy\) ka derivative sirf \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) likhna bohat aam ghalti hai; product rule zaroori hai. Aur bracket ke aage minus hai, to dono terms ka sign badlega.

Horizontal tangent ki shart
\[y - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 2x \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Kyun: fraction zero tab hota hai jab numerator zero ho (aur denominator zero na ho). Yeh ek line hai; ellipse ke jin points par yeh line guzarti hai wahi humare jawab honge.

(2) ko (1) mein rakhein
\[x^{2} - x(2x) + (2x)^{2} = 1\]
\[x^{2} - 2x^{2} + 4x^{2} = 1\]
\[3x^{2} = 1 \Rightarrow x = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: point ellipse par bhi hona chahiye aur shart (2) bhi poori karni chahiye, to dono equations saath hal kin. Square root lene par \(\pm\) dono aate hain, is liye do points milenge.

Points
(2) se: \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) ho to \(y = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\); aur \(x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) ho to \(y = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\).
Denominator ki jaanch:
\[2y - x = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} \ne 0\]
aur doosre point par \(-\sqrt{3} \ne 0\).
Kyun: agar denominator bhi zero hota to slope 0 nahi balke be-maani (undefined) hota. Yahan aisa nahi, is liye dono points sahi hain.

Tasdeeq
\(\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) par:
\[\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{4}{3} = 1\]
yani point ellipse par hai; doosra point bhi yahi values deta hai (minus times minus plus). Wahan horizontal tangents \(y = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) aur \(y = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) hain: yeh ellipse ka sab se ooncha aur sab se neecha point hain.
